items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: I had met an English fellow at the Trois Mailletz named Ronald Sweetman

ctx.x: My next thrill came in 1966 when I went to England for the first time to do a tour in that country. I had met an English fellow at the Trois Mailletz named Ronald Sweetman who was working in Paris and was a great jazz fan and record collector. He was also writing articles for different jazz magazines. When Ron eventually returned to England he told me that he was going to try and get me over there.

There was a regulation between the American Federation of musicians and the British musician's syndicate, whereby an American musician could play in England in exchange for an English one playing in the States. But that exchange didn't work for an American musician living in France. At one time I wanted to hire an English musician to work two weeks with
my band in exchange for me going there at a later date to work two weeks with an English group. But I was told by the person I had contacted that it was not possible.
